correctness.rationale: For an exterior vertex the only distances to landmarks are 1 and 2. A violating pair must disagree at every landmark, and uses at most two unused labels per axis. Thus capping each side at 7 is exact, not an extrapolation. Independently generated all 34 five-edge types by multisets of nonzero row neighborhoods and checked the original distance predicate on all nine representative boards. All nine types, conditions and stabilizers agree. Orbit–stabilizer gives 9/4 for the four 3×3 forms, 1/120 for the matching and q+5q(q−1) or its transpose for boundary forms. An independent direct check finds no equalizer with at most four cells on 5×5 and exactly 8430 with five; any smaller candidate on a larger board embeds in a 5×5 subboard whose obstructing pair persists. The nine-board orbit calculation also reproduces 17076 and 36720.
residual_risks: Exact executable enumeration and mathematical reduction, not formal machine verification. Axis swaps are intentionally excluded even on square boards.

value.rationale: The result resolves the structure and number of all optimal configurations for a natural two-factor graph family. It distinguishes the true boundary families from the stable types and supplies exact labeled orbit sizes; neither a matching construction nor the minimum value can give this information. The finite work is uniform over all board sizes.
residual_risks: Does not cover other rook board regimes or products with more than two factors.
